source.title: B2T Connection: Serving Stability and Performance in Deep Transformers
source.authors: Sho Takase; Shun Kiyono; Sosuke Kobayashi; Jun Suzuki

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests training stability in deep Transformers, extending depth and normalization findings to NLP and speech tasks rather than the convolutional benchmarks and identity shortcuts named in V3.
record.gate_note: Reports training success or failure for different Transformer methods and depths. BLEU, ROUGE, perplexity, and WER scores compare task performance, not training classification error, so they are not extracted as results for the claim. Figure-only loss curves are not assigned numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study measures training stability in Transformers with layer normalization and existing residual connections. It does not compare plain batch-normalized convolutional networks with identity-shortcut counterparts, as V3 specifies. Its normalization, initialization and task-performance comparisons also do not measure the effects specified in the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors attribute unstable deep Post-LN training to gradient attenuation through layer normalization, propose B2T to mitigate it, and report successful deep training with generally better task performance than Pre-LN. They acknowledge that B2T does not completely prevent vanishing gradients and that its behavior at extreme depths remains uncertain.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Transformer layer-normalization placement and adds a bottom-to-top residual connection; it does not use the original claim's random-initialization CIFAR classification setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcome varies with layer-normalization/residual configuration and depth: Post-LN fails in reported deep settings, while Pre-LN or B2T trains. The paper also states B2T does not fully prevent vanishing gradients in extremely deep Transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep Post-LN Transformers fail to train in the reported translation, summarization, language-modeling and speech settings, whereas Pre-LN and B2T configurations train successfully.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trainability of deep Transformers depends on layer-normalization placement and residual-connection design.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 3–5 attribute gradient attenuation to Post-LN layer normalizations and show mitigation with B2T. The limitations explicitly acknowledge remaining vanishing gradients.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual paths that bypass internal layer normalizations can mitigate gradient attenuation in deep Post-LN Transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C reports DeepNet failure with a small batch in 100L-100L training while B2T succeeds. Appendix D reports comparable task scores after removing internal layer normalizations and introducing scaling coefficients.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep Transformer stability and task performance depend on batch size and the combined normalization and residual-scaling recipe.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper reports training success or failure but not training classification error. Training stability evidence is empirical and task-specific; the authors say B2T does not perfectly prevent vanishing gradients and note limited computational budgets for 100L-100L comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported figure-only loss curves were entered as rows because the text gives no corresponding numerical values for those curves. Task-quality metrics were excluded because they do not measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error of large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and size or regularization effects.
Spurious local minima and extra student width in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
All specified comparisons: plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks, longer-training controls, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup residual networks.

Activation-matched initialization and signal propagation in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; orthogonal convolution kernels and trainable depth. Transformer initialization comparators do not isolate these effects.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature changes, catapult recovery and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the specified Fixup comparison. Layer normalization removal with B2T does not test these.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V3 limits_scope verdict: studying a related architecture is not evidence that V3 needs qualification. The row states above indicate inability to determine a specified claim effect, not uncertainty about the paper's explicit training-success or failure reports.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model-size effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Convolutional networks, ImageNet/CIFAR-10, identity shortcuts, and whether plain networks retain higher training classification error despite longer training. Tests depth and normalization-related training stability in Transformer architectures.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and plain-network trainable depth. T-Fixup is a comparator, but initialization effects are not isolated.
Learning rates above the stability threshold, curvature or sharpness, and loss recovery or divergence.
Batch normalization, speed of accuracy gain, and learning-rate tolerance. The tested normalization is layer normalization.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Deep Post-LN Transformers in tested machine translation, summarization, language modeling, and ASR settings
reader_labels.reason: Post-LN training failed at the reported deep settings, while Pre-LN and B2T trained successfully (R1–R13). The study tests Transformer stability, not the version's classification-error outcome or identity shortcuts.
